blocks.heading: The format
lines: Four jumbled sentences that make one paragraph. Type their order as a four-digit number, such as 4132.
Type-in answer, so a wrong answer costs nothing. Always type something.
Two in each CAT 2025 slot. Give each about 2 to 3 minutes.

blocks.heading: The method
lines: Read all four once and write a three to five word gist of each.
Find pairs you can prove. A pair is two sentences where the second can't stand without the first.
Join the pairs into one chain, then find the opener: the sentence that refers back to nothing.
Read the whole order once. If every join holds, type it.

blocks.heading: Clues that prove a pair
lines: A pronoun or "this", "that", "such" and the thing it points to.
A full name before the surname alone: "Elinor Ostrom" comes before "Ostrom".
A term introduced before it is used, and a general claim before its example.
"However", "yet" or "but" right after the view it turns against.
Dates and the order things happened in.

blocks.heading: Openers and closers
lines: The opener names its subject in full and doesn't lean on anything before it.
A sentence starting with This, But, Hence or Yet almost never opens.
The closer is often a conclusion (therefore, then, in short) or a consequence. Don't hunt for it first: pairs are more reliable.

blocks.heading: Traps
lines: Connecting words alone can mislead. Check that the meaning follows as well as the wording.
Two sentences that could each open: pick the one the other refers to.
A pair that reads well but leaves the other two with no place to go is the wrong pair.
After 3 minutes, type the order with the most proven pairs and move on.
